title: DAVE E2EE blocks voice receive in bot libs
description: Discord enforced DAVE E2EE on all voice channels on March 2, 2026. py-cord's start_recording() cannot decrypt DAVE-encrypted audio — hard-codes a RuntimeWarning and packet router crashes on every incoming packet. No Python or JS bot library currently supports the receive/decrypt side. Tracked upstream: py-cord #3139, discordjs #11419. All recording work is blocked until upstream ships a fix or we implement the Node.js recorder sidecar (see docs/plans/voice-recorder-sidecar.md).
close_reason: Resolved by implementing O Escriba (Node.js + dysnomia + @snazzah/davey), which handles DAVE decryption transparently. py-cord is no longer used for voice capture.

title: Async stop: immediate voice leave + background finalization + SIGTERM drain
description:
## Why
The current implementation blocks the HTTP response on WAV writes and AMQP publish — directly contradicting ADR-0003. The Game Master sees the bot still sitting in the voice channel while disk I/O and broker calls complete. The correct boundary: leave the voice channel synchronously (fast Discord API call), return 200 to Cronista immediately, then finalize in the background.

The SIGTERM handler is also missing session cleanup: it closes the AMQP connection and disconnects the Discord client but never stops active sessions, so any in-progress recording is silently lost on every redeploy.

## What needs to be done
**Async stop (recording.ts + session-manager.ts + server.ts):**
- recording.stop(): leave voice channel synchronously (disconnect, close receiver), set joined=false, return immediately — do not await finalizeWavs or publishTranscribeSession
- Expose a recording.finalize(): Promise<void> that closes write streams, patches WAV headers, and publishes the Celery task — to be called from background
- session-manager.stop(): call recording.stop() (sync part), delete session from Map, then kick off recording.finalize() as a background task (do not await on the HTTP path)
- server.ts: POST /sessions/:id/stop returns 200 as soon as session-manager.stop() resolves (i.e. after voice leave, before finalization)

**SIGTERM drain (index.ts):**
- On SIGINT/SIGTERM, call stop() on all active sessions to trigger voice leave
- Await all in-flight finalize() promises with a reasonable timeout (e.g. 30s) before calling process.exit
- If finalize times out, log structured warning with sessionIds and exit anyway

## Reference
- recording.ts:157–186 (stop, flushWavs)
- session-manager.ts:33–41 (stop)
- server.ts:61–82 (POST /sessions/:id/stop)
- index.ts:25–29 (shutdown handler)
- ADR-0003 (updated)

title: Fix appendPacket race condition in O Escriba
description:
## Why
appendPacket() is called as fire-and-forget (void) on every incoming opus packet. Because it awaits resolveUsername() before inserting into the speakers Map, multiple packets from the same user can arrive concurrently before the first await resolves. Each concurrent call finds speakers.get(userId) === undefined, creates its own local SpeakerState, and the last one to resolve wins — all PCM chunks collected by earlier calls are silently dropped.

This is also a hard prerequisite for the streaming-to-disk work (ADR-0004): with buffered chunks the race causes packet loss; with file write streams it would open the same path from two concurrent coroutines and corrupt the WAV.

## What needs to be done
- On first packet for a userId, synchronously insert a placeholder SpeakerState into the speakers Map using userId as a temporary username and create the decoder entry — before any await
- Resolve the real username asynchronously and update the username field on the already-inserted entry
- Ensure all subsequent packets for that userId are appended to the same SpeakerState regardless of whether username resolution has finished
- Unit test: simulate rapid concurrent packets for the same userId and assert no chunks are lost and the Map entry is only created once

## Reference
- recording.ts:197–221 (appendPacket, onData)
- ADR-0004 (streaming prerequisite context)

title: Slice C: O Escriba — capture Opus audio, write per-speaker WAVs, dispatch Celery task
description:
Implement full audio capture inside O Escriba. On stop: decode each speaker's accumulated Opus packets to PCM via OpusDecoder(48000, 2), write one WAV file per speaker to /data/recordings/{sessionId}/{userId}_{username}.wav, then dispatch a transcribe_session Celery task via RabbitMQ. Add RabbitMQ to docker-compose. See ADR-0003 for why O Escriba (not Cronista) dispatches the task.

- docker-compose.yml: add rabbitmq:3-management-alpine service; escriba depends_on rabbitmq

TESTS:

title: Enforce single-session invariant: Escriba 409 + Cronista guard
description:
## Why
If a /join request times out in transit (Escriba processed it, response never reached Cronista), Cronista has no _session_id but Escriba has a live session. When the Game Master retries /join, a new session ID is generated, Escriba starts a second session, and the first is orphaned permanently with no way to stop it. Cronista alone cannot defend against this because it cannot see Escriba's state after a network failure.

The fix is two-layered: Cronista guards the common case cheaply, Escriba enforces the invariant as source of truth.

## What needs to be done
**O Escriba (session-manager.ts + server.ts):**
- SessionManager tracks whether any session is currently active (a simple boolean or checking sessions.size > 0)
- POST /sessions returns 409 with { ok: false, error: 'session already active' } if a session is already running, regardless of the incoming sessionId
- The existing /health endpoint can optionally expose active session count for debugging

**O Cronista (voice.py — VoiceCog):**
- /join: if self._session_id is already set, respond ephemerally 'Já existe uma sessão ativa. Use /stop para encerrá-la.' without calling Escriba
- In _start_recording: if Escriba returns 409, treat it as 'session already running externally' — log a warning and surface a user-facing message ('O Escriba já está gravando. Use /stop para encerrar a sessão anterior.')
- This 409 path is the safety net for the lost-response scenario

**Tests:**
- Escriba: assert POST /sessions returns 409 when a session is active, assert it returns 200 when no session is active
- Cronista: assert /join responds with ephemeral error when _session_id is set, assert _start_recording handles 409 without raising

## Reference
- session-manager.ts (SessionManager.start)
- server.ts (POST /sessions route)
- voice.py:19–49 (join command, _start_recording)

title: Make RabbitMQ a soft startup dependency in O Escriba (ADR-0005)
description:
## Why
O Escriba crashes entirely at startup if RabbitMQ is unavailable (createCeleryPublisher throws at index.ts:18). This violates architecture principle #10 (fail independence): the Transcription Service being unreachable must not prevent O Escriba from recording. The Recording is far more valuable than the task enqueue — losing it because the broker is down is a disproportionate cascade. ADR-0005 mandates soft dependency.

## What needs to be done
- Wrap the createCeleryPublisher call in a try/catch at startup; if it fails, log a structured warning (including the RABBITMQ_URL and error message) and continue with taskPublisher = null
- TaskPublisher type is already nullable in SessionManager — null means 'no broker, skip publish'
- In the background finalization path (recording.finalize), if publishTranscribeSession fails (connection died mid-session), catch the error and log a structured message containing sessionId and the WAV file paths on disk, so an operator can manually re-enqueue
- Do NOT attempt automatic reconnection — that is a separate concern
- Unit tests: assert O Escriba starts and accepts /start requests when taskPublisher is null, assert finalize() logs and does not throw when publish fails

## Reference
- index.ts:18 (createCeleryPublisher — the crash site)
- celery-publisher.ts (TaskPublisher interface, createCeleryPublisher)
- session-manager.ts (taskPublisher already nullable)
- ADR-0005

title: Stream PCM to disk per-speaker during recording (ADR-0004)
description:
## Why
O Escriba currently buffers all decoded PCM chunks in RAM (pcmChunks: Buffer[] on each SpeakerState) and writes a single WAV file only at stop time. A 4-hour RPG session with multiple speakers can consume several gigabytes of RAM, and a process crash loses the entire session's audio. ADR-0004 mandates streaming to disk instead.

## What needs to be done
- Replace pcmChunks: Buffer[] with a per-speaker WriteStream opened at first packet arrival
- Write the 44-byte WAV header placeholder (all zeros) when the stream is opened
- Write each decoded PCM chunk directly to the stream — no in-memory accumulation
- At stop time, close all streams and seek back to patch the two WAV size fields (ChunkSize at byte 4, Subchunk2Size at byte 40) based on the actual file size
- Remove or repurpose flushWavs() — the new finalizeWavs() only closes streams and patches headers (no bulk write)
- Unit tests: assert WAV header is valid after finalization, assert file grows incrementally during recording, assert crash mid-session leaves a partially written but header-patchable file

## Dependencies
Depends on the appendPacket race fix — the synchronous stream open on first packet only works correctly once the race is eliminated.

## Reference
- recording.ts (Recording class, flushWavs, appendPacket)
- wav.ts (pcmToWav, writeSpeakerWav — both will need rework)
- ADR-0004
